Subject: Hosted API pricing — proposed commit tiers and PO options

Hi Jill,

Thanks again for the conversation earlier — it was great to hear more about Acme's rollout plan for Q3. Per our call I promised a concise summary of the two paths we typically use for hosted API customers: a straightforward usage-based (per-token) pricing with volume tiers, or a committed-usage contract (reserved monthly commit) that provides deeper unit discounts.

Quick summary (high level):
- Pay-as-you-go (no commit): standard per-token rates, billed monthly, net-30.
- Commit tiers (12-month): tier A: 0-1.5B tokens -> 8% off list; tier B: 1.5B-5B -> 18% off list; tier C: 5B+ -> 30% off list. True-up at month end; credits applied when commitment exceeded.

We can be flexible about invoice terms and PO formats — many enterprise customers use Acme-style preferred vendor forms. Two options that generally work:
1) Redwood signs Acme preferred vendor form and we bill per-token monthly (we accept PO + net-30 as standard).
2) If Procurement requires invoice + PO net-60 or special payment cadence, we can accept with a small financing uplift to cover extended payment (we typically add a 1.5% net-60 administrative fee unless contracted otherwise).

Please see the attached one-page commit summary I put together (RDW-ACME-commit-summary.xlsx). If you prefer, I can loop in our legal and finance leads to work directly with your procurement team.

Next steps: let me know which PO path procurement prefers (net-30, net-60 with fee, or vendor form signing) and I’ll coordinate internal approvals.

Best,
Rishi
Account Executive | Redwood Inference

Rishi,

Thank you — the tier breakdown is helpful. Procurement reviewed the commit summary and had two primary concerns before they can approve any preferred vendor agreement:

1) Acme requires our standard Preferred Vendor Form completed and signed (see attached). This includes PO on net-60 terms and a specific invoicing schedule (monthly invoices tied to a PO line item).
2) Our finance team will not accept a pricing structure that only manifests as "post-facto credits" unless the invoice clearly lists the discounted effective rate or there is a contract amendment that binds the discount to a PO schedule. In short, we need the discount reflected on the invoice/PO, not applied as a later credit.

Procurement is willing to move quickly if Redwood can: a) sign the attached preferred vendor form with net-60 accepted, and b) provide an invoice template that shows the committed-tier effective unit price per token (so we can match it to the PO line item).

If net-60 requires a fee on Redwood’s side, we need that spelled out so procurement can assess budget impact. Please advise.

Attachment: Acme_Preferred_Vendor_Form_2027.pdf (Acme standard preferred vendor agreement, 4 pages)

Thanks,

Rishi / Marissa —

Reviewed the preferred vendor form. Acme's asks are standard but the invoice/PO matching requirement is the sticking point. My recommended approach to keep this deal clean and compliant:

1) Contract schedule: Create a short exhibit (1 page) that enumerates the committed-tier effective unit prices for the duration of the PO/term. Language: "For the term of this Agreement, the Effective Unit Price for Tokens shall be the Committed Tier price set forth in Exhibit A. Invoices issued by Redwood shall reflect the Effective Unit Price per Token and shall be matched to Acme PO line items." This satisfies Procurement's need to see the price on the invoice.

2) Net-60: Avoid an automatic financing uplift in the vendor form if possible. If Finance cannot accept net-60 on open terms, propose a compromise: agree to net-60 with a one-time administrative fee (1.25% of the monthly invoice) for the first 3 months while credit terms are established, then revisit. Alternatively, accept net-30 in the vendor form and allow Acme to set a PO with net-60 on their side while we create an invoice matching cadence that triggers payment earlier (not ideal).

3) Accounting/back-end credits: Do not rely only on after-the-fact credits. If the commitment model is used, the exhibit should define the committed volumes and the Effective Unit Price so invoices show final prices (true-ups can be shown as reconciliations, but the invoice primary line should be the Effective Unit Price).

If you want, I can draft Exhibit A & the amendment language and circulate a redlined preferred vendor form. Marissa, can Finance confirm if 1.25% administrative fee for net-60 is acceptable operationally?

Regards,
Lauren Bishop
Head of Legal | Redwood Inference
lauren.bishop@redwood.ai

Next steps for us: procurement will queue the preferred vendor form once they have Redwood's redline (including Exhibit A) and an invoice template showing the Effective Unit Price. We'll aim to turn this around in ~7 business days after we receive the redline.

Jill
